<noinclude><pagequality level="1" user="" /></noinclude><section begin=par147 />{{GHGpar-heading|147|Incomplete Sentences}}

{{GHGmargin-letter|147|a}}
'''1.''' Sentences are called ''incomplete'', in which either the subject or the predicate or both must in some way be supplied from the context.<ref>This does not apply to such cases as {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=33|verse=8}}, where an infinitive with {{GHGheb|text=לְ}} appears alone in answer to a question, the substance of the question being presupposed as a main clause; cf. also {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=26|verse=7}}, where {{GHGheb|text=הִיא}} must again be supplied after {{GHGheb|text=אִשְׁתִּי}}.</ref> Besides the instances enumerated in {{GHGpar|116|s}} (omission of the personal pronoun when subject of a participial clause) and the periphrases for negative attributes {{GHGpar|152|u}}, this description includes certain (noun-) clauses introduced by {{GHGheb|text=הִנֵּה}} (see ''b'' below), and also a number of exclamations of the most varied kinds (see ''c'' below).

Rem. Incomplete sentences are very common in Chronicles, but are mostly due to the bad condition of the text; cf. Driver, {{GHGcite|title=Introd.}}<sup>6</sup>, p. 537, no. 27. Thus in {{GHGbible-ref|book=2 Ch|chapter=11|verse=22}}<sup>''b''</sup> restore {{GHGheb|text=חָשַׁב}}, with the LXX, before {{GHGheb|text=לְהַמְלִיכוֹ}}; in 35:21 add {{GHGheb|text=בָּ֫אתִי}}, with the LXX, after {{GHGheb|text=הַיּוֹם}} and read {{GHGheb|text=פְּרָת}} for {{GHGheb|text=בֵּית}}; in {{GHGbible-ref|book=2 Ch|chapter=19|verse=6}} and 28:21 the pronoun {{GHGheb|text=הוּא}} is wanted as subject, and in 30:9 the predicate {{GHGheb|text=יִֽהְיוּ}}; cf. also the unusual expressions in {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 Ch|chapter=9|verse=33}} ({{GHGbible-ref|book=Ezr|chapter=3|verse=3}}), {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 Ch|chapter=15|verse=13}} (''ye were not present?''), {{GHGbible-ref|book=2 Ch|chapter=15|verse=3}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=2 Ch|chapter=16|verse=10|hidebook=1}}, 12 (bis), 18:3.

{{GHGmargin-letter|147|b}}
'''2.''' The demonstrative particle {{GHGheb|text=הֵן}}, {{GHGheb|text=הִנֵּה|translate=en, ecce}} may be used either absolutely (as a kind of interjection, cf. {{GHGpar|105|b}}) before complete noun- or verbal-clauses, e.g. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=28|verse=15}} {{GHGheb|text=וְהִנֵּה אָֽנֹכִי עִמָּךְ|translate=and, behold! I am with thee}}; 37:7, 48:21, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ex|chapter=3|verse=13}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ex|chapter=34|verse=10|hidebook=1}}, or may take the pronoun, which would be the natural subject of a noun-clause, in the form of a suffix, see {{GHGpar|100|o}}. Whether these suffixes are to be regarded as in the accusative has been shown to be doubtful in {{GHGpar|100|p}}. However, in the case of {{GHGheb|text=הִנֵּה}} the analogy of the corresponding Arabic demonstrative particle ''ʾinna'' (followed by an accusative of the noun) is significant.<ref>On the same analogy any substantive following {{GHGheb|text=הִנֵּה}} would have to be regarded as originally a virtual accusative. Since, however, Hebrew does not possess case-terminations (as the Arabic does, and uses the accusative necessarily after ''ʾinna''), it is very doubtful whether, and how far, substantives following {{GHGheb|text=הִנֵּה}} were felt to be accusatives.</ref> If {{GHGheb|text=הִנֵּה}} with a suffix and a following adjective or participle (see the examples in {{GHGpar|116|p}} and ''q'') forms a noun-clause, the subject proper, to which {{GHGheb|text=הִנֵּה}} with the suffix refers, must, strictly speaking, be supplied again before the predicate.<ref>That these are real noun-clauses and that the participle (e.g. {{GHGheb|text=מֵת}} in {{GHGheb|text=הִנְּךָ מֵת}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=20|verse=8}}) cannot be taken as a second accusative (as it were ''ecce te moriturum''), is also shown by the analogy of Arabic, where after ''ʾinna'' with an accusative the predicate is expressly in the ''nominative''.</ref> Sometimes, however, the pronoun referring to the subject is wanting, and the simple {{GHGheb|text=הִנֵּה}} takes the place of the<section end=par147 /><noinclude>
<references/></noinclude>
